- m/z 185.042 (intensity 32.67) - this is quite intense, suggesting presence of chlorine or bromine
- m/z 186.045 (intensity 3.31) - M+2 isotope

The pattern with M+2 peak at about 32-33% of the base peak is characteristic of chlorine (Cl has two isotopes: 35Cl at 75.8% and 37Cl at 24.2%, giving an M+2 peak at about 1/3 of M peak for compounds with one Cl atom).

So the molecular ion is likely at m/z 183.045 and contains one chlorine atom.

- If we assume [M-H]- ion (ESI negative mode): M = 183.045 + 1.008 = 184.053
